question: Let \(\omega=-\dfrac12+\dfrac12 i\sqrt3.\) Let \(S\) denote all points in the complex plane of the form \(a+b\omega+c\omega^2,\) where \(0\le a\le1,\) \(0\le b\le1,\) and \(0\le c\le1.\) What is the area of \(S?\)
solution:
The useful relation is \(1+\omega+\omega^2=0\): it lets us make one coefficient zero without changing the point.

Direct calculation gives
\[
\omega^2=-\frac12-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}i.
\]
Thus \(1,\omega,\omega^2\) are unit vectors pointing at angles \(0^\circ,120^\circ,240^\circ\), and their sum is zero.

For any allowed triple \((a,b,c)\), let \(m=\min(a,b,c)\). Then
\[
a+b\omega+c\omega^2
=(a-m)+(b-m)\omega+(c-m)\omega^2.
\]
The new coefficients still lie in \([0,1]\), and at least one is zero. Therefore \(S\) is exactly the union of the three regions obtained by setting one coefficient equal to zero.

For example, setting \(c=0\) gives the filled rhombus with vertices \(0,1,\omega,1+\omega\). Its sides have length \(1\), and its height above the side from \(0\) to \(1\) is \(\sqrt3/2\), so its area is \(\sqrt3/2\). The other two regions are congruent rhombi.

These rhombi have no overlapping interiors: their nonzero points lie respectively in the angular sectors from \(0^\circ\) to \(120^\circ\), from \(120^\circ\) to \(240^\circ\), and from \(240^\circ\) to \(360^\circ\). They can share only boundary segments. Hence
\[
\operatorname{area}(S)=3\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}
=\boxed{\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
First let \(b\) and \(c\) vary; then adding \(a\) slides the resulting region horizontally by every distance from \(0\) to \(1\). This makes the boundary of \(S\) easy to find.

Write \(h=\sqrt3/2\). Since
\[
\omega=-\frac12+hi,
\qquad
\omega^2=-\frac12-hi,
\]
the points \(b\omega+c\omega^2\), with \(0\le b,c\le1\), fill the rhombus whose vertices are
\[
(0,0),\quad
\left(-\frac12,h\right),\quad
(-1,0),\quad
\left(-\frac12,-h\right).
\]

At any fixed height, this rhombus meets the horizontal line in an interval. Sliding by all \(a\in[0,1]\) extends that interval one unit to the right, with no gaps. Consequently, \(S\) is the filled hexagon with vertices, in boundary order,
\[
(-1,0),\quad
\left(-\frac12,h\right),\quad
\left(\frac12,h\right),\quad
(1,0),\quad
\left(\frac12,-h\right),\quad
\left(-\frac12,-h\right).
\]

The real axis divides this hexagon into two congruent trapezoids. Each has parallel sides of lengths \(2\) and \(1\), separated by height \(h\). Thus
\[
\operatorname{area}(S)
=2\left(\frac{2+1}{2}\right)\frac{\sqrt3}{2}
=\boxed{\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Slide a rhombus
